title: Enable Sunshine by its real unit name
head: f9b6743c2f49
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A successful canonical-unit install also registers a second Sunshine process in Hyprland autostart
leads.consequence: After the newly corrected enable succeeds, the installer writes o.launch_on_start("sunshine") even though the enabled user unit is WantedBy=graphical-session.target. At subsequent graphical starts two independent processes attempt to host Sunshine; the upstream RTSP server treats a failed bind as fatal. A partial/manual install that already has the autostart line is likewise not repaired. Use a single start path and remove old autostart lines, not merely stop adding new ones.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2 (double start via autostart append + graphical-session.target); published as the main finding

leads.summary: Older Sunshine installs with only sunshine.service cannot be re-run or removed using only the new hardcoded name
leads.consequence: For an already-installed old upstream-recipe Sunshine build whose unit is sunshine.service only, pkg-add skips upgrading it, then enabling the canonical app-* name fails under set -e, leaving subsequent setup incomplete. The remove path ignores the failed disable/stop and uninstalls the package, so it does not request stopping a running legacy sunshine.service. Check the unit actually installed, or provide an old-name fallback on install and on removal. This is conditional on users still having the old package or a compatible variant, not a claim that current Arch ships the old unit.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F5/F6 (pre-rename sunshine.service builds); no current channel serves one; kept private as too narrow

leads.summary: If tailscale0 is absent at install time, a successful install silently omits all Tailscale firewall allowances
leads.consequence: When Sunshine is installed before Tailscale, ip link show tailscale0 fails and the port-opening loop silently skips every Tailscale rule. The installer still reports that ports are open for Tailscale, and the later Tailscale installer does not invoke Sunshine firewall setup, so the tailnet stays blocked unless Sunshine is re-run. Add a follow-up on Tailscale install or a reconciler, or at least report the missing rules rather than claiming success.
leads.triage: factual, verified at head install script lines 34-36 and 88; pre-existing and unrelated to the changed lines; dropped

leads.summary: Sunshine install and remove are absent from both service menu sections
leads.consequence: The new working installer remains invisible to menu-only users despite manual/26-gaming.md:67 advertising its CLI route. Add install.service.sunshine beside install.service.tailscale at approximately line 228, with action omarchy-install-service-sunshine and disabled guard omarchy-pkg-present sunshine. Add remove.service.sunshine beside remove.service.tailscale at approximately line 312, with action omarchy-remove-service-sunshine and when guard omarchy-pkg-present sunshine. This missing registration predates this PR.
leads.triage: factual, verified: omarchy-menu.jsonc has tailscale but no sunshine install/remove entries; pre-existing, unrelated; dropped

leads.summary: The shipped remote plan still instructs implementers to keep the broken alias enable command
leads.consequence: Line 36 prescribes keeping systemctl --user enable --now sunshine when reworking this exact installer; following it would undo the canonical-unit fix. Update the literal command on line 36 to the packaged unit name, and update the now-historical old-command claim on line 9. This is documentation, not another executed path.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4 (plans/remote.md:9,36); published as Documentation note

leads.summary: Open PR #12271 changes the same Sunshine lifecycle and its test asserts an incompatible rerun path
leads.consequence: If #12271's security-floor helper and its Sunshine shell test merge while this PR's unconditional canonical enable is kept, that test's rerun assertion expects 'enable --now sunshine' but receives 'enable --now app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service' and fails. Conversely, wholesale replacement with #12271's installer replaces this PR's canonical-only rerun with its alias fallback. Explicitly reconcile the patches and their tests before merging, rather than using either version unchanged.
leads.triage: factual, verified in sol/pr12271-sunshine-install-test.sh (expects enable --now sunshine on re-run); Opus self-check confirmed against #12271 and noted its mock contradicts real systemd; published in overlap list with that qualifier. #12834 overlap (from hunt notes) verified via gh; published as merges-cleanly note

limits: Source-only hunt; no PR code, systemd manager, package manager, browser, network or fixture was executed. Behaviour of a real systemd user manager was left to the full reviewer.

Official Arch packaging GitLab clone was unavailable (authentication prompt), so this hunt confirms the current canonical and old-only unit layouts using Sunshine upstream tags v2026.516.143833 and v0.23.1 plus their upstream Arch recipes, not an official Arch binary file list or the installed version on any host.

Open #13230/#12505/#8879 duplicate the canonical enable fix; #12358 and #12472 change the same installer to remove duplicate autostart (merging one resolves H1 if its autostart deletion survives); #12834 touches the Sunshine Admin Exec and launcher, and its flag removal must survive resolution with this installer to avoid writing a shortcut rejected by its new launch guard. These are conditional merge interactions, not claims that all patches can merge unaltered. #12271's concrete conflicting test is H6.

H3 and H4 and part of H1 were pre-existing in the base; the now-successful canonical enable makes their user-visible consequences reachable on fresh installs. Prioritization is the maintainer's choice; the plan already calls out H1/H3/H4.

flags.claim: Several open PRs edit the same `systemctl` line in the installer, so merging one will conflict with the others (the list includes #12834 and #12472)
flags.why: #12834 does not edit the systemctl line. It changes only SUNSHINE_ADMIN_EXEC (base line 14), removing --ignore-certificate-errors, and it merges cleanly with this PR (merge-tree exit 0). #12472 changes the installer systemctl line to exactly this PR's text (`"$SUNSHINE_UNIT"`), so the installer merges cleanly (leaving a duplicate SUNSHINE_UNIT assignment at lines 8 and 17 of the merged tree). Its conflict with this PR is in the remover. The general 'merging one will conflict with the others' was only checked for pairs that include this PR.

flags.claim: Alternatively, combine this PR with one of the open PRs that already do this (#12358, #12472, #12271) [this = drop the autostart append and add a migration removing existing lines]
flags.why: All three stop the installer from appending the line, but only #12358 adds a migration (migrations/1789703649.sh) that removes existing lines. #12472 removes an existing line only when the installer is re-run (it swaps in disable_hyprland_autostart). #12271 only stops appending; its migration (1789400200.sh) is the security upgrade, and it does not clean up existing lines.

flags.claim: #12271's test expects a re-run to call `enable --now sunshine` through the alias. That test would fail if combined with this PR's unconditional real-name call.
flags.why: Both sentences are literally correct. The #12271 re-run assertion (test lines 168-171: grep -Fq 'enable --now sunshine') would not match `enable --now app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`. What is missing is that this expectation contradicts real systemd. The draft's own table row 3 (my run B2) shows `enable sunshine` after an enable by the real name fails with 'Refusing to operate on linked unit file'. #12271's mock systemctl returns 0 in that case (test lines 104-107). As written, the failure reads as this PR's fault, when it is the #12271 test that models impossible behaviour. #12271's alias branch (its installer lines 67-70) is only reached when /usr/lib/systemd/user/app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service is absent on the machine running the test, so that test also depends on the host.

flags.claim: With the PR, a re-run after a partial install completes: the package step is a no-op, the enable is idempotent, and the autostart append is guarded by `grep -Fxq`.
flags.why: The three listed reasons are verified (omarchy-pkg-add/omarchy-pkg-missing; run B3; install script line 68). 'Completes' also depends on the firewall step (sudo ufw allow for rules that already exist, then ufw reload) and the web app step on a re-run. Neither was tested, and the draft's own Test scope says firewall changes were not tested. My report recorded ufw re-run idempotency as not verified. My handback's 'Script flow' wording ('re-running after a partial install works') dropped that caveat, which is an inconsistency in my own report.

flags.claim: Sunshine treats failing to bind its ports as fatal (...), so one of the two copies is expected to abort.
flags.why: The source (14ffa6f and 63d35f7: nvhttp.cpp, confighttp.cpp, rtsp.cpp) logs at fatal level and raises the shutdown event, which is an orderly exit path. The source does not show an abort(). The SIGABRT comes from the reports in #7218 and #12349. 'Abort' in its plain-English sense is defensible, but the word 'so' ties it to the source.

flags.claim: before PR   install: enable sunshine ── fails ──▶ exit (no unit, no autostart line)
flags.why: 'No unit' suggests the unit is absent. The package and its unit file are installed at line 74, before the failure at line 75; the unit is only not enabled.

# RETRO: PR #13331

## What worked
- The boundary hunter and Opus converged independently on the double-start consequence (Sol H1, Opus F2), and on pre-rename packages (H2, F5/F6).
- The Opus self-check caught a real overstatement inherited from its own report: the merge-conflict set. It verified that with `git merge-tree` in its own clone. It also caught a claim missing a qualifier (the #12271 mock contradicting real systemd) and an untested re-run claim.
- Offline `systemctl --global --root` inside review.py reproduced both PR-body error messages exactly without a live user manager. This is a good reusable pattern for systemd unit-name PRs.

## Friction
- The `omarchy-reviewer` subagent's `report.md` write was refused by the harness ("Subagents should return findings as text"). Only `findings.json` persisted; the coordinator transcribed the hand-back into `opus/final-report-handback.md`. Suggest the agent definition allow report.md, or standardise on findings.json plus the hand-back text.
- Sol could not fetch the Arch PKGBUILD (GitLab auth); Opus established that Arch official has no `sunshine` package, so this was moot.
- `python-markdown` is not available; reader.html was rendered with a small inline converter.

## Process deviations
- The coordinator read `t1-13340-eea43555/{brief.md,completion.json,reader.html}` as format templates (coordinator only; nothing exposed to reviewers).

## Carry forward
- For PRs that unblock a previously dead code path, ask explicitly in the brief what newly reachable steps now run.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the unit-name fix is correct for the Sunshine builds Omarchy currently serves. Both failures described in the PR body reproduce with the old command, and the new command succeeds in each case. One existing installer step becomes reachable on fresh installs once this lands: Sunshine is then started twice at login (see below).

**Verified premises.** The `[omarchy]` repository's stable and rc channels serve `sunshine 2026.516.143833-4.1`, and edge serves `2026.914.233613-1`. Both packages ship exactly one user unit, `app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`, with `Alias=sunshine.service` and `WantedBy=graphical-session.target`, and no `sunshine.service` file. This matches upstream's `packaging/linux/app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service.in`. Arch's official repositories have no `sunshine` package.

**Verified behaviour** (offline `systemctl --global --root=<private tree>` with systemd 261.2 and the shipped unit file, so the same enable/disable code runs without a live user manager):

| State | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh | `enable sunshine` (old) | exit 1, `Unit sunshine.service does not exist` |
| Fresh | `enable app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service` (PR) | exit 0, alias and `graphical-session.target.wants/` links created |
| Already enabled | `enable sunshine` (old) | exit 1, `Refusing to operate on linked unit file sunshine.service` |
| Already enabled | PR enable again | exit 0, no change |
| Enabled | PR disable | exit 0, both links removed |
| Installed, not enabled | PR disable | exit 0, no-op |

With `set -e`, the old failure stopped the installer before the firewall rules, the Sunshine Admin web app and the autostart entry. With the PR, the `systemctl` step no longer stops a re-run after a partial install: the package step is a no-op, the enable is idempotent, and the autostart append is guarded by `grep -Fxq`. The firewall and web app steps on a re-run were not tested.

### Fresh installs now start Sunshine twice at login

The installer still appends `o.launch_on_start("sunshine")` to `~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua` (`bin/omarchy-install-service-sunshine`, lines 64-71 and 85). That helper runs `uwsm-app -- sunshine` when Hyprland starts (`default/hypr/helpers.lua:113-125`). It launches a second `/usr/bin/sunshine` process; it does not start the unit. The unit is also `WantedBy=graphical-session.target`, which the Omarchy session reaches.

```text
before PR   install: enable sunshine ── fails ──▶ exit (unit not enabled, no autostart line)
after PR    install: enable real unit ─▶ firewall ─▶ web app ─▶ autostart line
            login:   graphical-session.target ─▶ Sunshine unit      (copy 1)
                     Hyprland autostart ─▶ uwsm-app -- sunshine      (copy 2)
```

The login flow is derived from source reading and the linked issue reports; it was not exercised in a live login.

**Impact:** Sunshine treats failing to bind its ports as fatal (`src/nvhttp.cpp`, `src/confighttp.cpp`, `src/rtsp.cpp`), so one of the two copies is expected to exit. Issues #7218 and #12349 report this duplicate start at login, with one copy aborting. #7218 reports the unit copy restarting until systemd's start limit stops it. `plans/remote.md:9` already describes the double start. Which copy survives was not tested here.

**Suggested change:** keep the systemd unit as the only start path. Drop the autostart append from the installer and add a migration that removes an existing `o.launch_on_start("sunshine")` line. Alternatively, combine this PR with one of the open PRs that also stop appending the line: #12358 (which also adds a migration removing existing lines), #12472 (which strips an existing line when the installer runs) or #12271.

### Overlapping open PRs

Checked with `git merge-tree`, each of the following conflicts with this PR:

- #8879 makes functionally the same change in both scripts and adds `test/shell.d/sunshine-service-test.sh` (conflicts in both scripts).
- #13230 and #12505 fix the unit name in the installer only (installer conflict).
- #12358, #12472 and #12271 fix the unit name and also stop appending the autostart line. #12358 conflicts in the installer, #12271 in both scripts, and #12472 in the remover only (its installer line is identical to this PR's).
- #12271's test expects a re-run to call `enable --now sunshine` through the alias. Its mock `systemctl` accepts that, but real systemd refuses it once the unit is enabled (third table row above), so that test would need to change in a combined version.

#12834 changes the Sunshine Admin web app launch arguments in the same installer but merges cleanly with this PR.

**Documentation:** `plans/remote.md:9` and `:36` still give `systemctl --user enable --now sunshine`, and line 36 says the installer keeps that command. The PR body already notes this. Updating both lines keeps the plan consistent with the fix.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of both scripts at `f9b6743c`, systemd 261.2 `src/shared/install.c`, Sunshine upstream packaging, and the `[omarchy]` and AUR `sunshine` packaging. The two `[omarchy]` packages were downloaded (checksums matched the repository database) and their unit files extracted. Enable/disable was exercised offline in an isolated sandbox, and both scripts pass `bash -n`. Not tested: `--now` start/stop against a live user manager, a real login with both start paths, firewall changes, and the `sunshine-bin`/`sunshine-git` AUR variants (by source reading, both are built after the upstream unit rename).

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
